score_objections.objection: Sources show oversight letters to Meta/OpenAI, a COPPA-focused hearing, and a whistleblower-protection bill, but Grassley explicitly frames himself as pro-business/pro-growth, says government is only 'a referee', and stresses his bill does not upend NDAs or companies' confidentiality rights. Nothing in the sources supports structural rein-in measures (antitrust, breakup, broad platform mandates). The evidence supports targeted rules, not -2.

score_objections.objection: None of the six sources concerns regulating technology companies or Big Tech. The only adjacent item (SBA AI inventory letter) is federal-agency oversight, not tech regulation. Evidence is too thin for a -1 'Targeted rules' placement.

The single source is a one-sentence remark about a national lab supplying 'energy and critical materials to power the AI revolution'. It never mentions data centers, permitting, or conditions, so 'Build with conditions' asserts a nuance the evidence does not contain; if scored at all it reads closer to 'Build faster' than conditional support. Too thin for a position.

Both China sources are about SBIR/STTR grant due diligence and foreign-ownership vetting, not semiconductor export controls or chip sales. Hawkish direction is real, but the dimension as defined (export controls on chips) has no direct evidence; 'Leans hawkish' is an inference from adjacent China-tech-transfer positions rather than a chips stance.
